svg.text: NSX Federation objects behind the stretched management segment
Global Manager, stretched Tier-0 and Tier-1, RTEP tunnels, and where north–south traffic goes before and after a failover
primary location for the stretched gateways
secondary location · takes over after Network Recovery
NSX Manager cluster of the instance
NSX Manager cluster of the instance
eBGP · receives seg prefix, best path
RTEP on its own VLAN · MTU 1700
RTEP on its own VLAN · MTU 1700
no SR, no stateful services · follows T0 primary
seg-vcf-mgmt · created on the Global Manager · same subnet + gateway in both locations · VNI-A ↔ VNI-B stitched over RTEP

1 · Make the standby Global Manager active. 2 · Network Recovery: set Location B primary for the Tier-0 (the same-span Tier-1 follows). 3 · Tier-0 B now advertises the segment prefix without the prepend.

Nothing here is automatic: stretched gateways and the Global Manager do not fail over on their own (KB 441764, KB 444980). Until step 2, the segment is up on site B's hosts but has no north–south path (KB 412806).
